data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Safety and idempotence collapse into the same requirement for append-only log writers when replay mutates durable state: because the append is a mutation, the writer cannot be safe; and because at-least-once delivery can replay the append, the writer must be idempotent. But the deeper insight is that the log's append operation, viewed as a function on the log's logical content, is effectively a no-op on replay (the event is already there), so the writer achieves a quasi-safe property at the semantic level\u2014durable state is unchanged by replay\u2014even though the raw HTTP-level operation is not safe.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If dedup fails (race, lost idempotency key), the quasi-safety breaks and duplicate entries corrupt the log.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log intentionally allows duplicate physical entries (relying on consumers to dedup), the semantic-safety argument doesn't hold at the log layer.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"At the transport level, append is a mutation (not safe). At the semantic level, if dedup succeeds, replayed append becomes a logical no-op (safe). Thus the system engineer must build idempotence at the application layer to achieve safety at the semantic layer. The two properties are duals across abstraction levels: idempotence of the writer operation is the mechanism by which safety of the logical log state is achieved under replay.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
